fixture_name: Cloverleaf-to-urban interchange conversion — INT preliminary design (Wikimedia PD geometry)
subject: judge-baseline

justifications.substance: Shortened collector-distributor weave carrying a recorded 1,100 pcu/h design-year peak flow is a substantive, well-recognised preliminary-design safety mechanism (concentrated lane-change demand raising sideswipe/rear-end exposure), raised while geometry can still be changed.
justifications.evidence_grounding: Pivotal claim is anchored by the verbatim EV-IN-015 quote requiring junction-type suitability, channelling of conflicting streams, and lane balance/through-lane continuity, reinforced by EV-IN-004 and the recorded GA/volume inputs; no invented content.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Correctly typed as a safety_concern scoped to int:preliminary-design; the PIARC prompt application and HSM/IHSDM evaluation remain safety-analysis actions, keeping safety concern categorically distinct from any compliance assertion.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Specific and viable three-part action: apply the Appendix 1 §10.2 prompts now, quantify weaving adequacy via HSM Part C interchange models or IHSDM, then lengthen the weave or ramp-meter the entry if flagged — all feasible at preliminary design.
justifications.vru_coverage: Explicitly acknowledged as not applicable because the shared-use paths are grade-separated from the motorised weaving section, with road users correctly scoped to vehicle occupants.

justifications.substance: Uncontrolled free-flow ramp-terminal crossings of retained shared-use paths are a recognised, substantive VRU hazard directly relevant to this interchange scheme at preliminary design.
justifications.evidence_grounding: Pivotal normative claim is supported by verbatim EV-IN-016 and EV-IN-005 quotes and the layout/objective claims tie to recorded input facts; only the 'northern' terminal label lacks explicit grounding.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Correctly filed as a safety_concern categorically distinct from compliance questions, using PIARC checklist prompts as audit criteria, though calling question-form prompts 'requiring' mildly overstates their semantics.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Specific and actionable (thematic VRU audit, Walkability Checklist/CQSI tools, signalised or grade-separated crossings at both retained terminals) and viable at preliminary design despite mild solution prescription.
justifications.vru_coverage: Pedestrians and cyclists are the explicit focus, with their exposure at uncontrolled ramp-terminal crossings fully considered throughout the finding.
